title: Actions List (15)
path: Devices → Remote actions → Actions List (15)
user_intents: How do I configure Actions List (15)?
Where is the Actions List (15) setting?
What does Actions List (15) do?
text: Actions List (15) (Devices → Remote actions → Actions List (15)). Actions are immediate commands executed over the persistent channel — there is no polling delay. Pending marks commands not yet executed. The list spans information, messaging, power, security and maintenance. What it does Pick an action on the left and run it on this device. The Pending badge marks actions not yet executed. Action Effect Refresh Device information Pulls the latest parameters from the unit Send Message Shows a custom message on the device screen Ring / Buzz Device Plays sound to locate a nearby unit Reboot Device Restarts the device remotely Unlock Device Releases the screen lock Lock Device Applies the screen lock immediately Set Device Lease Expiry Sets the rental/lease end date for the unit Clear Failed Downloads Queue Drops stuck app/OTA downloads so they retry cleanly Trigger Collect Logs Pulls diagnostic logs from the device Uninstall an App Removes the specified package from the device Change Device Passcode Sets a new lock-screen passcode remotely Perform Factory Reset Wipes the device to factory state — irreversible Remove EMM Controls Unenrolls the device from management Send Shell Command Runs a shell command on the device Where to find it Devices → select → Action

title: Add via APK link
path: Apps → Add & Edit dialogs → Add via APK link
user_intents: How do I configure Add via APK link?
Where is the Add via APK link setting?
What does Add via APK link do?
text: Add via APK link (Apps → Add & Edit dialogs → Add via APK link). Adding starts with a link, not an upload. The portal fetches the APK, reads its metadata, and pre-fills the form — the admin’s job shifts from typing details to verifying them. 1. Paste a Download Link → Fetch App Details. Rules Enter a valid APK link that is directly downloadable. Google Drive and file-storage links are not supported — HTTPS only. See the Knowledge Base article for details. Signing Sign APKs with both v1 and v2 schemes, as Android recommends. Hosting Upload to your own web hosting (e.g. Amazon S3, GoDaddy). FieldX never hosts apps on the portal for security reasons; OneDrive, Google Drive and Dropbox links are not supported. Add dialog — paste a direct HTTPS APK link to fetch details.

text: Total Screen Time for the day (in Hours) (Device Usage Limits → Device Usage Limits → Total Screen Time for the day (in Hours)). What it does Sets a total daily screen-time budget. What does UEM vs MDM vs EMM do?
text: UEM vs MDM vs EMM (Concepts → Management basics → UEM vs MDM vs EMM). Overlapping names for the same idea at different widths. MDM (Mobile Device Management) covers phones and tablets. EMM (Enterprise Mobility Management) is Android-centered management with app and content controls. UEM (Unified Endpoint Management) stretches the idea to every endpoint — laptops, desktops, IoT. FieldX lives in the MDM/EMM space with UEM-style breadth: Android first, plus Apple and Linux fleets from the same console.

title: Updating an app
path: Apps → Push Apps → Updating an app
user_intents: How do I configure Updating an app?
Where is the Updating an app setting?
What does Updating an app do?
text: Updating an app (Apps → Push Apps → Updating an app). Updates are new builds of the same listing, not new listings. The platform guards this with signature matching, so a wrong-key APK can never silently replace a production app. 1. Increment the Version Code and sign with v1+v2 using the SAME keys as before. 2. Upload to your hosting, copy the link. 3. Push Apps → search the listing → Edit → replace the link → details pre-populate. Signatures must match If the signature hashes differ from the previous build, Save stays disabled. 4. Verify groups → Submit — devices update in a staggered rollout.

path: Concepts → Management basics → What is MDM?
user_intents: How do I configure What is MDM??
Where is the What is MDM? setting?
What does What is MDM? do?
text: What is MDM? (Concepts → Management basics → What is MDM?). Managing phones, tablets and other endpoints from a central console instead of touching each one. Enroll a device once; afterwards apps, settings, policies and updates go out over the air — to ten units or ten thousand. Every MDM product does three jobs: configure devices without handling them, secure company data on devices you don't fully own, and maintain fleets — updates, apps, health — at scale. Without MDM each change is manual labor per device; with it, one action covers the fleet.
